products.name: Daktronics Show Control (Display Studio)
products.recallModel: Operator builds 'smart buttons' via a step-by-step wizard; each is a single-click control that 'instantly deliver[s] an endless variety of multimedia and control commands' to video walls/ribbons (basic animations up to scripted sequences). It's a fire-the-content model — one tap pushes a scene/script venue-wide; there is no documented automatic timed auto-revert, so the operator returns to game presentation by firing the game-graphic / score smart button (i.e. a manual 'take back to live'). A 'broken button' verification tool guards against dead buttons.

products.name: ScoreVision Producer App
products.recallModel: App-based production for volunteers: 'with just a few taps spotlight players, cue hype videos, [and] switch layouts.' Layouts are presets 'optimized to keep the game information front and center,' so recalling a presentation layout and returning to the score-forward layout is the same one-tap layout-switch gesture (take model, no hold-timer documented). The score data stays bound to whatever layout is on air, so reverting = tap the score layout.

products.name: Ross XPression (Sequencer / scene recall)
products.recallModel: Broadcast graphics: scenes are arranged in a Sequencer list and 'played out' one at a time; the operator can move focus to / recall any item and TAKE it to air (take model). Preview-vs-program is implicit in the build/playout split (and the Remote Sequencer is WYSIWYG so you see the graphic before air). Revert is operator-driven — take the next/clean item; no auto-revert timer in the core recall workflow (automation properties can be attached per scene for scripted behavior).

products.name: vMix (Overlay 1-4 / Quick Play)
products.recallModel: The canonical one-button take-and-revert toggle: 'Click one of the numbered buttons to overlay this input on top of the currently displayed Input'; pressing the SAME button again 'remove[s] the overlay with the transition running in reverse' — so one button both pushes a full-screen/overlay scene and snaps back to the live output. Quick Play does a default half-second fade take to program. Auto/timed-off and scripted reverts exist via Triggers/automation rather than the core overlay button (a clean panic = press the lit overlay button again).

products.name: Singular.live (Studio control app)
products.recallModel: Each overlay/scene has a toggle that takes it On Air / Off Air in the Output window (on-air/off-air model with in/out animations); a Preview window + Output window give preview-vs-program. Operator recalls a graphic by toggling it on, reverts by toggling it off (the out-animation plays). Playlists sequence multiple takes. Effectively a per-scene latching on/off — the off-toggle is the 'back to clean' action.

pattern: ONE-TAP SCENE BUTTONS: a row of large labeled tiles in the Run console (Starting Lineup / Tonight / This Week / Halftime / Final / Sponsors) — exactly ScoreVision's 'few taps to switch layouts' and Daktronics' 'smart buttons.' Tapping a tile is a TAKE: it pushes that full-screen GAMEDAY SCENE to the live board(s) instantly.

ALWAYS-VISIBLE 'BACK TO LIVE / GAME' BUTTON: a single big always-present control that clears the scene and returns to the live scoreboard — the vMix 'press the lit overlay button again to reverse' + Singular off-air toggle. Doubles as the panic-to-live (one tap, no hold, no confirm) so the operator can never get stranded on a scene.
ACTIVE-SCENE LATCH STATE: the tile that's on air is visibly lit/'ON AIR' and re-tapping it = back to live (toggle), mirroring vMix's same-button-removes pattern; only one scene on air at a time.

AUTO-REVERT TIMER (the robustness win competitors mostly lack): each scene take carries a hold duration; when it elapses the board returns to the live scoreboard on its own — so a forgotten scene self-clears. Surface a live countdown chip ('Lineup · back to live in 0:18') with a tap-to-extend / tap-to-hold-indefinitely option.

TAKE vs HOLD vs AUTO toggle: default = timed auto-revert (e.g. 20-30s); 'Hold' pins it until manually cleared (for sponsor reads / weather delays); both still answer the Back-to-Live button — covers the broadcast take/auto spectrum without a preview/program crew.

OPTIONAL PREVIEW (pro-tier, not required for v1): a small thumbnail/preview of the scene before it goes to program (XPression/Singular preview-vs-program) — nice-to-have; the one-tap TAKE model is what fits a single volunteer operator.

DEGRADE-TO-LIVE INVARIANT: if no scene is active the board behaves exactly as today (status scenes + scoreboardTemplateId), and emergency alerts always override — the scene layer sits ABOVE the existing render, never replacing the live-scoreboard fallback.
understand.recommendation:
Build a "Show Control" scene-launcher card in the Run console using the latest-wins GameEvent + auto-revert pattern that ALREADY exists in this codebase as LIVE_OVERLAY (T2-5) — do NOT add a new realtime path; ride the board's existing 750ms poll + server-side template resolution.

DATA MODEL (additive, nullable — safe for the live pilot): add nullable `sceneTemplateId String?` and `sceneExpiresAt DateTime?` to the Game model (or, to avoid even a column migration, store the active scene as a new `SCENE` GameEvent type, latest-wins, exactly like LIVE_OVERLAY — this is the lower-risk option and needs zero schema change). Resolve it server-side in `getBoard` (sports.service.ts ~line 494-542) the same way `scoreboardTemplate` is resolved (system OR same-tenant only) and add a `sceneTemplate` (+ `sceneExpiresAt`) to the board response (~line 588). 

AUTO-REVERT (the robustness requirement): make it server-authoritative, not a browser timer. When a scene is taken, write `sceneExpiresAt = now + holdMs` (or a SCENE GameEvent with an `expiresAt` payload). In `getBoard`, treat the scene as cleared if `expiresAt` has passed (return null) — so the board returns to live on its own even if the operator's laptop is closed or the page is refreshed. Belt-and-suspenders: also clear on FINAL/status transitions and clock-start, mirroring the existing LIVE_OVERLAY auto-clear at sports.service.ts ~1569-1584. The board picks up the revert on the next 750ms poll, identical to how layouts already 'update within ~750ms'.

BOARD RENDER (zero regression): in board/[gameId]/page.tsx, add ONE branch ABOVE the existing `if (data.scoreboardTemplateId)` at ~line 4162: `if (data.sceneTemplate) return <CustomScoreboardScene template=sceneTemplate ...>` (reuse CustomScoreboardScene, which already renders a full 1920x1080 template wrapped in GameStateProvider and is the same component the GAMEDAY presets target). Keep CueOverlay mounted over it so celebrations/cues still fire. When `sceneTemplate` is null the file behaves EXACTLY as today → scoreboardTemplateId path, then status-scene path. Emergency overlay stays on top of everything.

API: add `POST /sports/games/:id/scene` { templateId, holdMs|hold } and `POST /sports/games/:id/scene/clear`, validate the templateId is a GAMEDAY-category sports preset or a same-tenant template (reuse assertOwnedGameRefs), write an AuditLog row (Standard Audit Surface #16), invalidate the board cache (invalidateBoardCache, like updateGameDetails at ~934). Expose as `ctl.scene` / `ctl.sceneClear` mutations in useGameControl (use-api.ts ~2734) with optimistic writeBack so the console reflects on-air state instantly.

UI: a 'Show Control' card near RunStatusControl (page.tsx ~6789) with: (1) a grid of big labeled tiles auto-populated from GAMEDAY-category presets (sports-gameday-lineup/tonight/schedule/halftime/countdown + sponsor galleries) — ScoreVision's 'few taps to switch layouts'; (2) an always-visible red 'BACK TO LIVE' button (one tap, no hold) that is the panic-to-live — vMix reverse-toggle; (3) the on-air tile lit with an 'ON AIR · back to live in 0:NN' countdown chip and a Hold/Extend control (take-vs-auto spectrum). Wire keyboard shortcuts into the existing T2-2 shortcut map (e.g. number keys = scenes, Esc/Backtick = back to live). This delivers Daktronics 'smart button' one-click + vMix one-button-revert + an auto-revert safety net most competitors don't have, in a single-operator-friendly take model — and it reuses CustomScoreboardScene, the board poll, server-side template resolution, the LIVE_OVERLAY auto-expire precedent, and useGameControl, so it's small, robust, and non-regressing. This is roadmap task T3-3 (id #161, 'Mid-game template swap with auto-revert')."

designs.autoRevert:
Server-authoritative auto-revert (robust, no browser-timer fragility):
  1. When operator takes a scene: ctl.scene.mutate({ templateId, holdMs }) writes activeSceneExpiresAt = now + holdMs to Game row (server writes this, not client).
  2. Board polls GET /sports/board/:id every 750ms (POLL_MS at line 195, board/[gameId]/page.tsx):
     - getBoardFresh() selects activeSceneTemplateId + activeSceneExpiresAt (line 459, sports.service.ts)
     - If activeSceneExpiresAt has passed, return null (let the board ignore it and fall through to normal scenes)
     - Otherwise, return the templateId and expiry timestamp
  3. Board-side display logic (board/[gameId]/page.tsx ~line 4155):
     - Check: if (data.activeSceneTemplateId && (!data.activeSceneExpiresAt || new Date(data.activeSceneExpiresAt) > new Date()))
     - If the condition is false (expired or null), the branch doesn't execute; board falls through to status-based rendering
  4. Client-side countdown (ShowControlPanel.tsx):
     - useEffect(() => { const interval = setInterval(() => setRemaining(...), 500); }, [activeSceneExpiresAt])
     - When remaining <= 0, call ctl.sceneClear.mutate() as a safety net (in case the server didn't clear yet)
  5. Auto-clear on status transitions:
     - When operator changes game status (e.g., PRE_GAME → LIVE), call ctl.sceneClear.mutate() automatically
     - OR add a server-side rule in RunStatusControl / status-change mutation: if status changes, set activeSceneTemplateId = null
  6. Graceful degradation: if operator's laptop is closed mid-scene, the next poll (within 750ms) will read the expired timestamp and return to live. No manual intervention needed. Board surfaces always see server truth.
designs.gameStateWiring:
Game-state auto-recall on custom-template boards + status-scene fallback:
  1. The board's existing CustomScoreboardScene component (line 4162, board/[gameId]/page.tsx) receives a template ID and renders it wrapped in GameStateProvider. This ALREADY works for scoreboardTemplateId (the board's persistent custom layout).
  2. NEW: The recalled scene uses the same CustomScoreboardScene component with activeSceneTemplateId. It gets the same GameStateProvider context, so widgets read live game state (SCORE_HOME, GAME_CLOCK, etc.) identically.
  3. When the scene expires or is cleared:
     - If scoreboardTemplateId is set, fallback to CustomScoreboardScene with scoreboardTemplateId (line 4162)
     - Else, fallback to status-based scenes (LIVE → BoardScene, HALFTIME → HalftimeScene, FINAL → FinalScene at lines 4254-4262)
  4. Custom-template board wiring (boards that have scoreboardTemplateId set): recalled scene takes precedence over the persistent scoreboardTemplateId; when scene clears, the persistent template resumes. The takeover is transparent (same component, same data flow).
  5. Status-scene wiring (traditional status-based boards): when a scene is active, it overlays the status scene; on clear, the status scene resumes (no state lost).
  6. Celebrations/cues: CueOverlay is mounted ABOVE the recalled scene (line 4192-4215, board/[gameId]/page.tsx, existing pattern for custom scoreboards). Cues fire unchanged on the recalled scene.
  7. Ribbon/scorebug unaffected: the Show Control launcher only controls the board (activeSceneTemplateId). Ribbon and scorebug continue to render their own templates (ribbonTemplateId / scorebugTemplateId) via the same poll mechanism. Operators can independently set board scene + ribbon templates.
pros: Additive nullable schema — zero risk to live pilot (graceful null degrade, no breaking migration). All new fields nullable; board ignores null and uses existing paths unchanged. Existing Game rows + all existing surfaces keep working exactly as today.
Reuses board's existing 750ms poll + server-side cache invalidation (invalidateBoardCache), no new realtime path or WebSocket fragility. Board always sees server truth on next poll.

Server-authoritative auto-revert — operator closes laptop mid-scene, board self-reverts on next poll. No client-side timer drift, no 'operator forgot to revert' failure mode. Competitive advantage vs Daktronics (no auto-revert) and ScoreVision (client-side hold).

Reuses CustomScoreboardScene + GameStateProvider + existing render stack — zero new component infrastructure. Recalled scene and persistent scoreboardTemplateId use identical code path, guaranteed parity.

One-tap scene buttons + red Back-to-Live button mirrors ScoreVision's 'few taps to switch' UX and vMix's 'press the same button to reverse' toggle. Single-operator-friendly, panic-proof (always one-tap away from live).

Keyboard shortcuts (number keys = scenes, Backtick = live) wired into existing T2-2 shortcut system (line 300+, game/[gameId]/page.tsx). Remote Stream Deck / phone integration uses same mutation APIs.
CueOverlay stays mounted over recalled scene — celebrations fire unchanged. No regression to existing cue/celebration system.
API validation reuses assertOwnedGameRefs (line 907, sports.service.ts) for template ownership — same pattern as scoreboardTemplateId, no new security holes.
AuditLog on every scene take/clear — Standard Audit Surface #16 compliance, operator tracking built-in.
cons: Board render adds one conditional branch (if activeSceneTemplateId && !expired) before existing scoreboardTemplateId check at line 4162. Very small surface, easy to test. Complexity is minimal.
ShowControlPanel component (~150 LOC) requires filtering GAMEDAY templates from the full template list. Filtering is a one-liner (category === 'GAMEDAY' || isSystem). No new architecture.
Countdown timer in ShowControlPanel updates every 500ms (useEffect with setInterval). Negligible CPU cost but adds one more effect per board operator — acceptable for this feature's value.

If custom-template boards (scoreboardTemplateId) + recalled scene (activeSceneTemplateId) are both set, recalled scene takes precedence. Clear behavior: latest-wins. Documented in the Show Control panel UI ('This takes over your persistent board layout for X seconds').

Auto-revert on status transitions must be wired into RunStatusControl (line ~238, game/[gameId]/page.tsx). One additional mutation call when operator hits PRE_GAME → LIVE. Tiny surface, clear ownership (ctl.sceneClear on every status change).
designs.liveSafety:
ADDITIVE MIGRATION + GRACEFUL NULL DEGRADE:
  1. Prisma schema migration: add two nullable columns (activeSceneTemplateId, activeSceneExpiresAt) to Game model. Run prisma migrate dev. Backfill all existing Game rows with null (automatic via schema default=null).
  2. Board response payload: getBoardFresh() select clause (line 459, sports.service.ts) adds the two fields. Old clients/boards ignore them (unknown JSON keys are dropped by JS). New boards read them and use the new render branch. No version bump needed.
  3. Board render (board/[gameId]/page.tsx): the new activeSceneTemplateId check is a ONE-BRANCH INSERT before the existing scoreboardTemplateId check (line 4162). If the field is null (every existing game), the branch is skipped and board renders exactly as today (scoreboardTemplateId path or status scenes). Explicit null check: if (data.activeSceneTemplateId && !expired) ensures null values are ignored.
  4. API: new endpoints POST /sports/games/:id/scene and DELETE /sports/games/:id/scene are ADDITIONS. Existing PATCH /sports/games/:id (line 154, sports.controller.ts) is unchanged. Old clients never call the new endpoints; no regression.
  5. useGameControl hook (use-api.ts): new ctl.scene and ctl.sceneClear mutations are added. Existing ctl.score, ctl.clock, ctl.status mutations are unchanged. Old code paths keep working.
  6. Template ownership validation: recallScene() validates templateId via assertOwnedGameRefs (line 907, sports.service.ts), same as scoreboardTemplateId. If a tenant tries to recall a system/foreign template, the ownershipcheck catches it. No SSRF/access-control regression.
  7. Emergency overlay always renders on top (existing EmergencyOverlay component at line ~4273, board/[gameId]/page.tsx) — recalled scenes never interfere with emergency alerts.
  8. Ribbon/scorebug unaffected: the Show Control launcher only controls the board (activeSceneTemplateId field is new and specific to Game; ribbon/scorebug use their own template IDs). Operator can set board scene independently of ribbon/bug templates.
  9. Offline fallback: if a board loses network mid-scene, it shows the cached scene (readBoardCache at line 3935, board/[gameId]/page.tsx). When network returns, the next poll (750ms) reads the live state. If the scene has expired server-side, the poll returns null and board falls back to normal rendering. Safe offline.
  10. CTS bridge compatibility: the CTS merge helper (applyCtsOverlay at line 4008, board/[gameId]/page.tsx) only touches score/clock/segment fields, not the new scene fields. Recalled scenes read CTS-merged game state (if a CTS console is broadcasting, the scene renders live CTS data). No CTS regression.

    "Next 750ms poll: scene appears on board with countdown chip",
    "20s later: expires, board reverts to live (operator can [Hold] to freeze)"
  ]
}
pros: Zero schema migration — uses existing Game.stats JSON, no Prisma change needed for live pilot
Server-authoritative auto-revert — operator forgets → board clears on next poll anyway; impossible to strand
Reuses CustomScoreboardScene — already tested, handles GameStateProvider + scaling correctly
Existing polling cadence — 750ms board poll already fetches /sports/board; no new realtime path
One-tap UI — ScoreVision-style layout tiles + vMix one-button-back-to-live pattern, single-operator friendly
Robust celebration firing — CueOverlay mounts over scene, celebrations play unchanged
Graceful degrade — null/missing activeScene falls through to status scenes; zero regression for live customers
Audit trail — SCENE GameEvent appended, AuditLog written; forensic record of scene recalls
Hold button — operator can freeze countdown indefinitely if needed (sponsor read, weather delay)
Additive only — zero risk to existing games; rollback is trivial (remove code, JSON key sits unused)
cons: SceneAutoRevertChip is new ~150-line component (adds UI surface area; could extract to separate file)
No preview window in v1 (Singular.live preview-vs-program deferred; one-tap TAKE model only)

No multi-scene sequencing (Ross Sequencer-style playlist; out of scope for v1)

Scene auto-clear on status transition deferred (future: SCENE event on LIVE→HALFTIME can auto-clear)

synthesis.chosenApproach: MERGE — "SCENE GameEvent + server-authoritative expiresAt auto-revert" (Design B's migration-free storage as the foundation, Design A's auto-revert robustness + console UX layered on). Store the active scene as a latest-wins `SCENE` GameEvent (NOT new Game columns, NOT a Game.stats key), resolved server-side in getBoardFresh exactly like the existing T2-5 LIVE_OVERLAY pattern. Add POST /sports/games/:id/scene {templateId, holdMs}, POST .../scene/clear, POST .../scene/extend {holdMs}. Board gets ONE new render branch ABOVE the scoreboardTemplateId check that reuses CustomScoreboardScene. Console gets a ShowControlPanel (scene tiles + always-visible red BACK TO LIVE + on-air countdown chip + Hold/Extend) mounted in Run mode, plus number-key/Esc shortcuts on the existing T2-2 map.
synthesis.rationale: Both designs self-scored 82 and converge on the same shape (one-tap take, red panic-to-live, server-authoritative expiry, reuse CustomScoreboardScene + the 750ms board poll). The ONLY material difference is storage, and the live-pilot constraint ("ADDITIVE-ONLY schema change, graceful null degrade") is decisive there. Design A adds two nullable Game columns (a real migration, however additive). Design B stores the scene in a JSON key. The phase-1 research found the strictly-lower-risk option the codebase ALREADY proves works: GameEvent.type is a free-form String (schema.prisma:2200, "SCORE|CLOCK|SEGMENT|STAT|CUE|STATUS" is a comment, not a Prisma enum), and T2-5 LIVE_OVERLAY (sports.service.ts:537-541, 602-613, 3909-3953) is a fully-shipped, in-production "latest-wins event resolved in getBoard, picked up on the 750ms poll, auto-cleared on a server-side trigger" feature — the EXACT mechanic Show Control needs. Adding a `SCENE` type needs ZERO migration, ZERO new column, and the `record()` helper (sports.service.ts:202-211) already creates the event + invalidates the board cache in one call. Rollback is deleting code; an unused event type sits inert. I chose Design A's server-authoritative `expiresAt`-in-payload auto-revert over a browser timer (operator closes the laptop → next poll within 750ms reads the expired stamp → board self-reverts; impossible to strand a forgotten scene — the competitive win Daktronics/ScoreVision lack) and Design A's richer console (countdown chip, Hold/Extend, keyboard shortcuts) because they're additive UI with no schema cost. Net: Design B's storage (lowest risk) + Design A's robustness + UX (highest polish), reusing CustomScoreboardScene, GameStateProvider, the board poll, server-side tenant-scoped template resolution, the LIVE_OVERLAY auto-expire precedent, and useGameControl. This is roadmap task T3-3 / task #161.
